messages:
emily: FYI we started getting a customer SLO alert for 5xx spikes on hosted inference around 20:04 UTC. Multiple tenants reporting timeouts and gateway 504s.

ravi: seeing same in metrics — queue latency jumping, provision queue backlog. KEDA scaledobjects show short bursts but pods not Ready for 30-60s.

sasha: any recent infra deploys?

emily: no infra deploys in last 12h. We did push a model onboarding change earlier but should be isolated.

jordan: pulling logs from autoscaler: `ScaledObject` poll shows successful scale requests but HPA desired != current for 3 consecutive cycles. readiness checks failing on new pods: `model-init timed out` and `auth token fetch 503` intermittent.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2923456789 - Hosted API 5xx spike (autoscale lag). Pager assigned: sasha.

sasha: prioritizing customer-facing mitigation. Suggested short-term: increase min replicas for affected nodepool, and set KEDA cooldown to 30s to avoid repeated rapid scale triggers.

emily: can we confirm auth token service YAGNI rate limit? support-ops, any billing throttles?

support-ops: we had a billing API outage earlier (20:00-20:12) — rate-limited background token refresh for some tenants. That might explain the auth token fetch 503s during pod init.

ravi: that matches — pods try to fetch customer creds during init; if token fetch fails, container stays in Init state ~45s before retrying. With many pods initializing, the kube scheduler backlog causes request queues to grow -> gateway 504s.

sasha: reproduction steps so we can validate fix:
1) Deploy a small deployment with init that calls internal billing/token service on start.
2) Simulate rate limit on token endpoint (HTTP 429/503).
3) Trigger a burst of requests to cause KEDA to request scale 20->200.
4) Observe pod readiness time and HPA desired/current lag.

emily: repro confirmed in staging. Two root causes: (A) dependency on synchronous token fetch during init delays Ready; (B) KEDA ScaledObject polling interval is low and combined with HPA stabilization/window produced many concurrent coldstarts that contended for our token service.

jordan: proposed immediate mitigations:
- Roll out a hotfix to change init to async token fetch with permissive fallback cached token for init path (reduces init time).
- Temporarily raise minReplicaCount on the scaledobject for hosted-api to 10 for the next 2h.
- Increase KEDA pollInterval from 30s -> 60s and disable burst-scale for tenant pools while we remediate.

support-ops: rolling account-level token cache for init now (staging tested).

oncall-bot: Runbook note added: "autoscale-init-token-dependency". Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscale-init-token-dependency

sasha: also adding a short-term HPA patch to reduce readiness probe strictness during warmup (allow 2 failed checks before marking NotReady). Code snippet for KEDA ScaledObject patch:

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:\n  name: hosted-api-scaledobject
spec:\n  scaleTargetRef:
    name: hosted-api-deployment
  pollingInterval: 60  # increased from 30
  cooldownPeriod: 30
  minReplicaCount: 10
  triggers:
  - type: prometheus
    metadata:
      serverAddress: http://prometheus.k8s.svc
      metricName: redwood_queue_backlog
```

ravi: note: we should be careful with minReplica bump to not exceed reserved GPU capacity for Dedicated customers. Ops, verify capacity before apply.

emily: Ops confirmed availability in region-us-west-2 for a 2h bump. Proceeding to apply patch in 2m.

support-ops: patch applied to scaledobject in us-west-2, minReplicaCount=10, pollingInterval=60. Observing metrics now — queue backlog dropping and 5xx rate reducing.

jordan: logs show new pods now passing init within ~6-8s after async token fix. auth token 429s dropped after we applied backoff/retry and local cache.

sasha: customer-facing update: prepared a short note explaining we had a cascading token service rate-limit that amplified scale-up delays; mitigation applied (minReplica bump + KEDA poll interval + init async token). Ready to send when 15m stable.

emily: monitoring window 20m. If stable by 20:35 we'll close.

oncall-bot: Automation: created rollback job to revert minReplicaCount after 2 hours.

support-ops: customers on the affected tenants reported degraded UX but no data loss. Raised follow-ups with Billing team to add capacity and circuit-breaker on token endpoint.

jordan: follow-up action items:
- [P0] Add local token provisioning path to runtime so pod init doesn't block on external token service.
- [P1] Update KEDA docs/runbook to recommend pollInterval >= 60s for bursty workloads.
- [P1] Add HPA stabilization window tuning for model-init paths.
- [P2] Investigate autoscaler telemetry to detect init-blocking dependencies sooner.

emily: thanks everyone. I'll post a post-incident note after 24h.

sasha: closing notes: stable at 20:33 UTC; 5xx rate back to baseline. Will open a follow-up JIRA for Billing fixes and autoscaler hardening. :white_check_mark:
